subject: Inference operational profile & model recommendation for Hightower
messages:

Subject: Intro + quick ask on token profile before kickoff

Sara — great to meet earlier today. As discussed, we want to lock down a concise inference operational profile before the technical kickoff so Dev and Grace can scope the onboarding sprint. Two quick asks to help us prepare:

1) Typical prompt + expected response length (average tokens) and any max context you expect to use (e.g., 8k, 16k).
2) Hourly/peak QPS expectations and an example daily traffic shape (are you bursty at 10am PT or steady all day?).

If you already have a spreadsheet with example calls, token counts, or sample prompts, please attach — that will let Dev produce a short model shortlist and sizing estimate before the kickoff.

I copied Grace (CS lead) and Lauren (onboarding) so we can align on rollout/contacts. We’re targeting a 2-week implementation sprint after kickoff if the profile looks like what we discussed.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Intro + quick ask on token profile before kickoff
Attachments: hightower_token_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Aditya — thanks, attaching the token profile spreadsheet (lightly redacted). A few notes from our side:

- Average prompt length: ~120 tokens. Typical responses average 260 tokens. We have a small set (~5%) of long-chain prompts where responses can be 1,500–2,000 tokens (these are debug/reporting flows).
- Max context required for product features: 32k tokens for our historical conversation lookback; most flows use 8k.
- Peak patterns: daily peak between 11:30–13:30 ET driven by scheduled batch enrichment. Peak QPS for interactive calls ~25–40 QPS for a 1-minute window; sustained interactive QPS is ~6–8.
- Estimated avg daily active requests: 40k/day.

We flagged the debug/reporting flows as candidates for an async batch pipeline if that makes sense for cost. Miguel — looping you in for any clarifications on context length.

Best,
Sara Klein
Head of Product, Hightower Analytics
sara@hightower.ai
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Klein <sara@hightower.ai>
Date: 2027-10-17T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Draft model shortlist + preliminary sizing for Hightower (v1)
Attachments: model_shortlist_v1.pdf (PDF), MAP_draft.docx (Mutual Action Plan draft)

Hi team — I looked through Sara’s token profile and sketched an initial shortlist and sizing rationale. High level: we should offer two serving tiers so Hightower can balance cost vs long-context requirements. See attached PDF for the compact table; key points inline below.

Shortlist (recommended):
- Variant A (low-cost): quantized LLaMA-2-70B-fp8-qa (8k context) — good for 95% of interactive traffic; minimal latency, best unit-cost.
- Variant B (long-context): RedLM-32k (specialized long-context optimized kernel) — for the 5% long-chain reporting flows that need 32k.
- Fallback C: smaller 13B tuned for snappy responses in low-latency endpoints (for any microservice that cannot tolerate SLO breaches).

Sizing estimates (very rough, per day baseline):
- Interactive tier (Variant A): 38k calls/day, avg 380 tokens/call => ~14.4M tokens/day. Peak QPS buffer: provision for 50 QPS sustained for short bursts.
- Long-context batch (Variant B): 2k calls/day, avg 5.5k tokens/call => ~11M tokens/day (but can be scheduled/batched overnight).
- Combined 25.4M tokens/day ~ 760M tokens/month.

Operational notes:
- Recommend prefix/KV caching for common prompts (we can precompute for templated flows).
- Canary plan in MAP: start with 5% traffic on Variant B for reporting flows, validate quality and latency, then shift remaining scheduled runs to batch slot if cost high.

Open questions for kickoff (short):
1) Can Hightower tolerate asynchronous batch for the 32k flows or does product need sub-15s latency?
2) Are there any regulatory constraints (PII retention limits) for cached KV?

I’ll be at the kickoff to walk through the MAP and kernel/quantization tradeoffs.

—Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sara Klein <sara@hightower.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-18T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Handoff + onboarding plan (kickoff prep)

Thanks, everyone — good detail in the token profile and Dev’s draft. From CS side I want to capture a concise handoff so engineering can hit the ground running on Monday. Actionable items below:

1) Confirmed scope for sprint-0 (2 weeks):
   - Week 1: infra + model routing config (Variant A baseline + Variant B scheduled batch routing), KV cache policy, and testcase prompt set; canary config ready by Friday.
   - Week 2: canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100% for non-reporting flows), monitoring dashboards, and regression checks against the provided prompt set.

2) Required inputs from Hightower before kickoff (please send by EOD Friday):
   - Final list of 10 canonical prompts for quality gating (we’ll run evals).
   - Confirmation on whether 32k flows can be async-scheduled or need interactive latency ≤15s.
   - Any IP/retention constraints for caching (Dev will implement conservative defaults if none supplied).

3) Risk & mitigations:
   - Cost risk: long-context interactive calls are the main driver — we’ll instrument token counters and alert at 20% over forecast.
   - Availability risk: provide fallback routing to the 13B microvariant when Variant A latency exceeds SLO.

4) Tentative kickoff: Monday 2027-10-18 10:00 PT — calendar invite forthcoming (Grace will own daily stand).

Please reply inline if that plan looks wrong or add any constraints I missed.

Thanks — I’ll circulate a one-page kickoff checklist and the MAP doc to sign off.

Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
From: Miguel Torres <miguel@hightower.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Klein <sara@hightower.ai>
Date: 2027-10-18T13:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Handoff + onboarding plan (kickoff prep)

Thanks Grace — quick clarifications from our side:

- The long 32k flows are used by our audit/reporting engine and must be completed within 60s; async nightly batch is acceptable for historical reprocessing but not for real-time audit checks. That implies we need a small portion (approx 300 calls/day) to be interactive at up to 32k context.
- On peak QPS: earlier numbers were conservative — we expect possible spikes to 80 QPS for up to 90s during market open-type jobs; please ensure burst capacity or graceful throttling.
- Cost question: can you provide a rough delta in monthly inference cost if 300 interactive 32k calls remain interactive vs moved to batch? A ballpark estimate is fine for procurement.

Miguel
CTO, Hightower Analytics
miguel@hightower.ai
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Torres <miguel@hightower.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Sara Klein <sara@hightower.ai>
Date: 2027-10-19T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Handoff + onboarding plan (kickoff prep) — final sizing note
Attachments: hightower_onboarding_sizes.csv (CSV)

Great clarifications, Miguel — summarized and updated the sizing with the interactive 32k requirement included. Key numbers (finalized for kickoff):

- Interactive Variant A (8k baseline): 37.7k calls/day, avg 380 tokens/call => 14.3M tokens/day.
- Interactive 32k (reporting/audit): 300 calls/day, avg 8.5k tokens/call => 2.55M tokens/day (these must remain interactive).
- Scheduled batch 32k (non-time-sensitive): 1.7k calls/day, avg 5.5k tokens/call => 9.35M tokens/day.
- Combined total: ~26.2M tokens/day = ~786M tokens/month.

Estimated cost delta (very rough): keeping 300 interactive 32k calls vs moving them to batch increases monthly inference spend by ~12–18% due to higher per-token serving premium and the lower batching efficiency for interactive calls. We’ll include this in the MAP as a decision point for procurement.

Action items before kickoff:
- Hightower: share 10 canonical prompts + confirm any retention/KV constraints.
- Redwood (Dev + Grace): finalize canary config and model routing rules; prepare cost projection slide for procurement.

See attached CSV for the per-call breakdown. Looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Onboarding Program Manager, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
